content.text:
`addMonths` in `dates.js` now clamps to the last day of the target month, so Jan 31 + 1 month gives Feb 28 instead of Mar 3.

**The cause:** `setMonth` doesn't clamp. Jan 31 with the month set to February becomes "Feb 31", which rolls over into March.

**The fix:** the function now sets the date to the 1st, moves the month, then sets the day to the smaller of the original day and the target month's length. The time of day is kept and the input is not mutated.

I also added `dates.test.js` with 8 cases: mid-month dates, Jan 31 → Feb 28, the leap-year case (Feb 29), 31 → 30 in a 30-day month, negative offsets, year rollover, and time-of-day/no-mutation. Two of the cases are from the code comment at the top of `dates.js`.

🧾 1 receipt · npm test → # pass 8

Things I didn't check:
- I only have `dates.js` in this folder. If the billing code calls something other than `addMonths` to compute the next billing date, that path would still be wrong. The billing code isn't here, so I couldn't check it.
- The folder is not a git repository, so there is no diff to review. The changes are just the two files above.
